hero_alt: The Virupaksha Temple gateway and smaller stone shrines of Hampi among boulder hills in Karnataka, India
q: Is Hampi worth visiting, and how do I get there?
answer: Hampi in Karnataka is the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara Empire (14th–16th century) and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986. It lies about 340 km (211 miles) from Bengaluru; the nearest railway station, Hosapete Junction, is about 13 km (8 miles) away. Go October–February and allow three days. We arrange it by private car with driver — price on request.
facts: of ruins in the Tungabhadra basin

sections.h2: What Hampi is — and why it is worth the journey
paras: The Group of Monuments at Hampi was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1986. In the words of the Archaeological Survey of India, it holds the remnants of the capital city of the last great Hindu kingdom of Vijayanagara, from the 14th to the 16th century.

The site is huge: about 4,188 hectares (roughly 10,350 acres) in the basin of the Tungabhadra river, in what is now Vijayanagara district (formerly part of Ballari). Temples, halls, gateways and royal buildings sit among hills of piled granite boulders — a landscape that looks like nowhere else in India.

Hampi is far from India's big cities, and that is both the challenge and the reward. You need to plan the journey, but once you are there the pace is slow: early walks, temple courtyards, river views and sunsets over the boulders.

items: Virupaksha Temple
Its entrance gateway rises about 50 m (160 ft) in nine tiers — the landmark you see from all around.
Vijaya Vittala Temple
Famous for the 56 musical pillars of its Ranga Mantapa and the Stone Chariot in the courtyard — the same chariot shown on India's 50-rupee note.
Lotus Mahal
An elegant pavilion with lotus-shaped arches, one of Hampi's best-known royal buildings.
Hemakuta and Matanga hills
Hemakuta Hill has groups of small temples above Virupaksha; Matanga Hill is the classic sunrise viewpoint — go with care, and no climbing in the dark.
The giant Ganeshas and Lakshmi Narasimha
Kadalekalu and Sasivekalu Ganesha, and the monolithic Lakshmi Narasimha, carved from single boulders.
Coracle rides
Karnataka Tourism lists round coracle boat rides on the river. Follow local guidance on river levels.

sections.lead: Karnataka Tourism suggests about three days. Most of our guests reach Hampi from Goa or Bengaluru and continue to the other — a natural loop through South India.

What to know
rows: Hampi is about 340 km (211 miles) from Bengaluru — a full day by private car, with breaks.
The nearest station is Hosapete Junction, about 13 km (8 miles) from Hampi. Many visitors take an overnight train from Bengaluru; check current trains on IRCTC.
Many travellers add Hampi after a Goa stay, by private car. It is a long day — we plan the stops.
The nearest airports are small regional ones with few flights; most visitors come by overnight train or by road from Bengaluru or Goa.

sections.h2: When to go: season and Hampi Utsav
items: October to February
The best months, as Karnataka Tourism advises. Hampi gets very hot outside October–February.
Hampi Utsav (Hampi festival)

From 2026 the festival is held every year on 3, 4 and 5 November instead of February (Government of Karnataka, Feb 2026). The 2027 edition is expected on 3–5 November — confirm before you plan around it.
Walk early and late
Start at sunrise, rest in the middle of the day, and go out again for the late-afternoon light. Carry water.
Health
Hampi gets very hot outside October–February; walk early and late, carry water, and consult your doctor or CDC / NHS Fit for Travel.

sections.text: Monuments with a ticket charge foreign visitors a separate rate; buy at the counter or on the ASI site. Opening hours and fees change — confirm before travel (as of Nov 2026). For your visa: apply yourself only at the official site indianvisaonline.gov.in — beware look-alike sites that charge extra. We are not a visa agency. In November 2026 the Government of India announced that the Tourist Visa is being renamed the Visitor Visa (PIB, 11 Nov 2026); until the official site changes, apply for the visa it shows there.

faqs: For travellers who love history and landscapes, yes. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara Empire (14th–16th century), spread over about 4,188 hectares among granite boulders. It is far from the big cities, so plan about three days to make the journey worth it.
How many days do I need in Hampi?
About three days, as Karnataka Tourism suggests. One day is not enough for a site this large; three days lets you see the main temples in the cooler hours.
How do I get to Hampi from Bengaluru or Goa?

Hampi is about 340 km (211 miles) from Bengaluru — a full day by private car, or an overnight train to Hosapete Junction, about 13 km (8 miles) from Hampi. From Goa, most travellers go by private car. We plan the stops.
What is the nearest railway station to Hampi?
Hosapete Junction, about 13 km (8 miles) away. Check current trains on IRCTC.
What is the best time to visit Hampi?
October to February. Hampi gets very hot outside those months, so walk early and late and carry water.
From 2026 the Hampi festival is held every year on 3–5 November instead of February, as announced by the Government of Karnataka in February 2026. Confirm the 2027 dates before you travel.
Why is Hampi a UNESCO site?
The Group of Monuments at Hampi was listed in 1986 as the remnants of the capital of Vijayanagara, the last great Hindu kingdom of South India, from the 14th to the 16th century.
